thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: Severity=high — GPU pool 'inference-eu-west-1' effective capacity down 48% (queue growth). Auto-scale attempts failing. Thread opened 2109876543

ashok: reading the alert — seeing queue backlog on the api-facing router. Paging oncall. I'll start triage.

maria: I'm on it. quick check: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-eu-west-1 -o wide` shows several nodes NotReady. attaching snippet:

```
NAME                           STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-eu-12                      Ready      <none>   42d   v1.27
gpu-eu-13                      NotReady   <none>   3d    v1.27
gpu-eu-14                      NotReady   <none>   6h    v1.27
gpu-eu-15                      Ready      <none>   12d   v1.27
gpu-eu-16                      NotReady   <none>   2h    v1.27
```

samir: nvidia driver logs on gpu-eu-13 show repeated Xid errors and NVML failing to initialize. excerpt:

```
[2026-03-14T22:10:03Z] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[2026-03-14T22:10:04Z] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID 4321: process abort
[2026-03-14T22:10:04Z] nvml: failed to query device: NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN
```

ashok: autoscaler logs? why didn't it replace those nodes?

maria: autoscaler shows scaling attempted but then aborted: `maxNodesReached` for that pool according to cloud provider. Logs:

```
2026-03-14T22:12:01Z autoscaler: desired=40 current=40 max=40 -> abort scale up (quota / pool limit)
2026-03-14T22:12:01Z autoscaler: queueLen=1840 pendingRequests=600
```

jess: customer impact check — metrics show increased 95th p99 latency for hosted-gen endpoints in eu-west-1 and a 12% request error spike for premium customers. Tagging support to prepare comms.

ira: oncall for infra will be 30 min. @ashok handing over; leaving notes.

ally: we should consider throttling non-critical workloads and diverting traffic to other regions if capacity can't be restored fast. can we temporarily rate-limit free-tier?

samir: confirmed many pods are stuck in Terminating on NotReady nodes. `kubectl describe pod` shows container runtime lost connection. We can force-delete pods but that will shift load to other nodes.

ashok: immediate plan:
1) reduce non-prod traffic via rate limit (ally)
2) attempt remote driver soft-restart on NotReady nodes (maria+samir)
3) if nodes stay NotReady, cordon & drain then reprovision/replace (maria)
4) request a temporary increase to pool capacity/quota with cloud (ashok)

maria: starting with a soft restart on gpu-eu-13 and gpu-eu-14: `ssh root@gpu-eu-13 'systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && systemctl restart docker'` — logs show driver coming back, but then Xid 62 appears repeatedly.

samir: xid 62 = GPU page fault / driver memory issue. stacktrace shows a leaking kernel module after yesterday's driver package 535.101. Repro on 3 nodes. I'm rolling back to 535.86 on a single node to test.

deploy-bot: deploy rollback requested by samir for package=driver-535.86 -> env=inference-eu-west-1 [ci job: 1291]

ashok: while rollback runs, we need to keep the autoscaler from misreporting. I see it uses node readiness as capacity signal; when nodes are NotReady they still count towards `current` because cloud provider hasn't finished deleting resources. we can work around by lowering the autoscale pool target to avoid `maxNodesReached` blocking. contacting cloud ops.

ally: rate-limit rules applied: free-tier reduced to 20% qps in eu-west-1. monitoring for error reductions.

samir: rollback applied to gpu-eu-13 (test node). after reboot and driver install, `nvidia-smi` shows devices healthy, NVML OK. Running a small load test — holding for 5m.

maria: draining gpu-eu-14 (still flapping) -> `kubectl drain gpu-eu-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` then cloud instance replacement requested.

ashok: cloud support responded: increase in reserved quota possible but takes ~45m. they've queued the request. meanwhile we should free up nodes by evicting non-critical pools.

jess: Customer comms draft: "We are investigating GPU capacity issues affecting inference in eu-west-1. You may see higher latencies or throttling for non-critical workloads. We're mitigating and will update in 1 hour." Approval? :eyes:

ira: +1 send to affected customers list; ops-team to include ETA once cloud quota update confirmed.

samir: test node steady for 12m, no Xid after rollback. pushing rollback to two more nodes (gpu-eu-12 and gpu-eu-16).

maria: after rolling restarts and draining 2 bad nodes, pool effective capacity back to ~82%. queue length dropping from 1840 -> 420 over 18 minutes. autoscaler now able to spin up replacements once quota increases.

deploy-bot: cloud quota increase granted to pool 'inference-eu-west-1' +8 nodes at 2109879***. autoscaler reports desired=44 current=40 -> scaling to 44.

ally: lifting free-tier throttle to 50% while monitoring.

jess: support: record of affected customers for follow-up: acct-112, acct-198, acct-403. severity=high; customer impact: increased latency / limited throughput for ~55 minutes during peak.

ashok: handoff notes for next oncall (ira):
- root cause likely driver regression (535.101) causing repeated Xid / NVML failures.
- immediate mitigation: rollback driver on remaining fleet, cordon+replace nodes still flapping, temporary quota bump and rate-limits for non-critical traffic.
- follow-ups: postmortem, driver package gating in staging, add NVML health probe to node-exporter to trigger faster reprovisioning.

ira: acknowledged. I'll follow up with postmortem owner assignment. good job team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident CLOSED (mitigated) — effective capacity restored to 95% after replacements and rollback. total duration 00:59:00.

ashok: quick retrospective items: add automated rollback if >3 Xid events in 10m; add alert on autoscaler `maxNodesReached` with page to cloud-ops. I'll create tickets.

maria: filing initial incident ticket and assigning owner for postmortem: samir -> will include timeline, metrics, and customer impact.

samir: got it. I'll include replication steps for driver regression and propose a canary plan for driver upgrades.

jess: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and credits as needed.
